body:
## Problem

Finding class: dependency-vulnerability. go.mod pins golang.org/x/text at v0.39.0 — the version raised during implementation to clear GO-2026-5970 — but GO-2026-6629 (High) is fixed only in v0.41.0.

## Evidence

Detecting tools: grype 0.120.1 (`grype dir:.`: golang.org/x/text v0.39.0 GO-2026-6629 High, fix 0.41.0) and govulncheck 1.9.0 (`-show verbose` lists GO-2026-6629 among the advisories in required modules not called). go.mod:41 `golang.org/x/text v0.39.0 // indirect`. `go mod why -m golang.org/x/text`: internal/ui → charm.land/glamour/v2/ansi → golang.org/x/text/cases.

## Impact

The module is linked into every release binary; govulncheck finds no call path today, but the same reachability caveat applies as for x/net, and non-reachability scanners report the release as carrying a High advisory.

## Fix

`go get golang.org/x/text@v0.43.0 && go mod tidy` (v0.41.0 is the lowest fixed version; v0.43.0 is current), then `mise run all` and `grype dir:.` to confirm 0 matches for golang.org/x/text.

## Resolution
golang.org/x/text raised to v0.43.0. grype dir:. reports 0 matches; govulncheck reports no vulnerabilities; mise run all green.
title: golang.org/x/text v0.39.0 has an unfixed High advisory (GO-2026-6629)

body:
## Problem

Store text is sanitized in findings.Store.add (load.go:159-170) and then rendered by glamour in renderBody. Goldmark decodes numeric character references (``, ``, ``) while rendering, so a body containing no raw control byte comes out of renderBody with raw ESC and BEL. bubbletea v2's cell renderer (ultraviolet styled.go:121-126, `passThrough`) forwards every terminated DCS, APC, SOS and PM sequence to the terminal unchanged; it drops only OSC (except OSC 8) and non-SGR CSI. Sanitize-at-load is therefore not the "single choke point" its comment claims.

## Evidence

Reproduced with renderBody (dark style, width 80): body `hello ]52;c;aGVsbG8= world` renders as `\x1b[38;5;252mhello \x1b]52;c;aGVsbG8=\a\x1b[m…` — a complete OSC 52 clipboard write in the output string. ultraviolet@v0.0.0-20261008173134-6b8d4baf91b4 styled.go:121-126: `if !ansi.HasApcPrefix(seq) && !ansi.HasDcsPrefix(seq) && !ansi.HasSosPrefix(seq) && !ansi.HasPmPrefix(seq) { return false }; return terminated(seq)`. The existing end-to-end test (detail_test.go TestDetailNeverRendersStoredEscapes) covers raw and JSON-escaped bytes only, not character references.

## Impact

A finding body in a cloned repository can send DCS/APC/SOS/PM sequences to the user's terminal by spelling ESC as `` and ST as `\`. Example: tmux's passthrough DCS (`ESC Ptmux; ESC ESC ]52;c;<base64> BEL ESC \`) delivers an OSC 52 clipboard write to the outer terminal when passthrough is enabled; DCS status requests make some terminals answer on stdin. The README's promise that a cloned repository cannot control the terminal through the store is false.

## Fix

Sanitize the rendered output, not only the input: after `r.Render(body)`, drop every escape sequence except SGR (`CSI … m`) and OSC 8, walking the string with charmbracelet/x/ansi's parser (already in the module graph through lipgloss). Apply the same filter to the "render failed" fallback. Add an end-to-end test that loads bodies with entity-encoded OSC 52, DCS (`P…\`) and APC through findings.Load, opens the detail view, and asserts View().Content contains no ESC that does not start an SGR or OSC 8 sequence. Update the comment at load.go:159.

## Resolution
detail.go: renderBody passes glamour's output (and the render-failed fallback) through keepStyling, which keeps only SGR (CSI…m with no prefix/intermediate), OSC 8 and newlines, using charmbracelet/x/ansi's DecodeSequence. Tests: TestKeepStyling (OSC 52, DCS, APC, CSI 2J, private CSI ending in m, BEL) and TestDetailDropsEscapesDecodedFromEntities (entity-encoded OSC 52, tmux DCS passthrough, APC through Load and View). Real-terminal check: entity payload shows no OSC 52, DCS or BEL. load.go comment corrected.
title: Markdown character references reintroduce terminal escapes after Sanitize

body:
## Problem

openPicker puts the cursor on the current value with `p.list.Select(at)`. When typing narrows the list, bubbles replaces the filtered items without clamping the cursor, so `SelectedItem()` returns nil and updatePicker's Accept branch returns as if nothing matched — while matching rows are on screen.

## Evidence

Reproduced: with the default `state: open` filter, press `s` (cursor on "open", index 1), type `fix`: visible rows `["  fixed (2)"]`, SelectedItem "" and index 1; `enter` leaves mode = picker and Sel = map[state:open]. model.go:338 `p.list.Select(at)`; model.go:349-352 `it, ok := m.picker.list.SelectedItem().(pickerItem); if !ok { // Nothing matches what was typed. return m, nil }`. The picker tests pass because the lens/category cases start with the cursor on row 0 ("all").

## Impact

Type-to-jump-then-enter, the picker's main interaction, fails for every facet that already has a value selected — including the state picker in the default configuration. The user sees a match, presses enter, and nothing happens.

## Fix

After forwarding a key to the picker list and after delivering a list.FilterMatchesMsg to it, clamp: `if m.picker.list.SelectedItem() == nil && len(m.picker.list.VisibleItems()) > 0 { m.picker.list.Select(0) }`. Add a test: `s`, type `fix`, `enter` → mode list, Sel[state] == "fixed", 2 rows visible.

## Resolution
model.go: clampPicker selects row 0 when the cursor is past the narrowed rows; called after every key and every filter result delivered to the picker. Test TestPickerEnterAfterNarrowingFromSelectedValue (s, type fix, enter → state fixed, 2 rows). Real-terminal check: state: fixed · 2/8.
title: Picker ignores enter after typing narrows below the current value's row

body:
## Problem

resize calls `m.search.SetWidth(width - 4)`, which is negative for widths 0-3. The textinput then panics while rendering its placeholder in the list view.

## Evidence

model.go:174 `m.search.SetWidth(width - 4)`. Reproduced: WindowSizeMsg{Width: 0, Height: 0..3} followed by View() panics with `runtime error: makeslice: len out of range` (bubbles textinput.go:748); Width 3 panics with `slice bounds out of range [:1] with capacity 0` (textinput.go:752), stack through model.go:159 (View). Picker and detail modes do not panic at the same sizes; width ≥ 4 does not panic.

## Impact

The program crashes, leaving the alternate screen, when a pane is squeezed to ≤ 3 columns or when the pty reports a width of 0 (some non-interactive or freshly created ptys do on start). TestDetailSurvivesTinyTerminal checks width 10 in detail mode only.

## Fix

`m.search.SetWidth(max(width-4, 0))` (width 4, i.e. SetWidth(0), renders). Add a table test that sends WindowSizeMsg for widths 0-5 and heights 0-3 in list, picker and detail modes and calls View() for each.

## Resolution
model.go resize: m.search.SetWidth(max(width-4, 0)). Test TestTinyTerminalsDoNotPanic renders widths 0-5 x heights 0-3 in list, picker, detail, warnings and search modes. Real-terminal check: alive with the window resized to 3 columns.
title: Program panics when the terminal is 3 columns wide or less

body:
## Problem

Three statements contradict the implementation: README.md:66-69 says symlinks inside the store are skipped and that a cloned repository cannot use the store to control the terminal or to read files outside the store; CLAUDE.md:54-57 says only regular files are read and every symlink is skipped; load.go:159-160 calls Store.add "the single choke point between store content and the terminal".

## Evidence

Markdown character references reach the terminal as escapes after Store.add (finding "Markdown character references reintroduce terminal escapes after Sanitize", detail.go:50-60); symlinked `<auditor>/open` directories and store-path components are followed (finding "Symlinked open directories and store-path components are followed", load.go:67-79, main.go:85-116).

## Impact

Users and contributors rely on a security guarantee that is false, and an agent following CLAUDE.md treats Store.add as sufficient sanitizing when changing the renderer.

## Fix

Fix the two code findings and then re-verify these three statements against the new behaviour; if either code fix is deferred, reword the statements to what the code does (state that rendered markdown is filtered to SGR and OSC 8 only, and which symlinks are refused).

## Resolution
The two code findings are fixed, and README.md (store-content paragraph), CLAUDE.md (hostile-clone, never-write and parser rules) and the load.go clean() comment now describe the actual protections: sanitize at load plus keepStyling on rendered output, and symlink refusal inside the store and in its path.
title: README and CLAUDE.md promise store-content protections the code does not provide

body:
## Problem

Sanitize keeps `\n` and `\t` (needed in Body) and is applied identically to every field, so a ledger title, id, area or category — JSON strings that may contain `\n` — draws extra lines in the list. Sanitize also keeps Unicode format characters: it removes only `unicode.IsControl` (Cc) runes, so bidi overrides such as U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE and U+2066-U+2069 isolates (category Cf) reach the screen.

## Evidence

load.go:162-166 applies `Sanitize` to all twelve fields; sanitize.go keeps `r == '\t' || r == '\n' || !unicode.IsControl(r)`. Reproduced: a ledger record whose title contains 26 `\n` produces a 45-line View() at height 20; a following line of the title renders as its own row `CRITICAL  injected row`, and the second real finding and the help line fall off-screen. model.go:33-39 (item.Title/Description) format the fields without stripping line breaks.

## Impact

Store content can draw fake list rows and push real findings and the help line off-screen; in bidi-capable terminals (e.g. VTE-based) override characters reorder a title's visible text. Display spoofing only — no terminal control — but it defeats the list as an accurate account of the store.

## Fix

In Store.add, for every field except Body replace `\n`, `\r` and `\t` with a space after Sanitize. In Sanitize, also drop U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069. Tests: a ledger title with `\n` loads as one line; a title with U+202E loads without it.

## Resolution
load.go clean(): every field except Body goes through oneLine (newline and tab → space) after Sanitize; warnings too. sanitize.go drops U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069. Tests TestLoadFlattensSingleLineFields and three Sanitize bidi cases (written as UTF-8 byte escapes so the source holds no raw bidi character).
title: Single-line fields keep newlines, and bidi controls pass Sanitize

body:
## Problem

Only the store root's entries and the `.md` entries inside `open/` are type-checked. A symlinked `<auditor>/open` directory is followed by `fs.ReadDir` (os.Root allows symlinks that stay inside the root), and a symlink in the path to the store itself (e.g. `docs` → elsewhere) is followed by `os.Stat` in findStore (main.go:92) and by `os.OpenRoot(dir)` (main.go:109). findings.py refuses both (`_symlink_in_store`), and README/CLAUDE.md say symlinks are skipped.

## Evidence

load.go:68-69 `dir := path.Join(auditor, StatusOpen); entries, err := fs.ReadDir(fsys, dir)` with no Lstat. Reproduced: `a/open -> ../b/open` loads b-1 twice (once as auditor "a", path a/open/b-1.md) with no warning; a repository with `docs -> ../outside/docs` loads finding x-1 titled "OUTSIDE" with no warning, while findings.py `iter_open` returns [] with "refusing to follow a symlink". README.md:66-69 and CLAUDE.md:56-57 state symlinks are skipped.

## Impact

A cloned repository can make the browser list a store from another location on the machine, or the same findings under a second lens, with no warning — the opposite of what the docs promise and of what the store's own tooling does.

## Fix

In loadOpen, `fs.Lstat(fsys, dir)` before ReadDir and skip a symlink with a warning. In findStore, Lstat each path component from the candidate store up to the directory that contains `.git` (or up to the start directory when there is none) and refuse a symlinked component with an error naming it, as findings.py does. Tests for both.

## Resolution
load.go loadOpen: fs.Lstat on <auditor>/open and skip a symlink with a warning. main.go findStore: refuseSymlinks Lstats docs, docs/audit and docs/audit/findings under the found project and errors on a symlink. Tests TestLoadSkipsSymlinkedOpenDir and TestFindStoreRefusesSymlinkedComponent.
title: Symlinked open directories and store-path components are followed

body:
## Problem

The loader claims to mirror findings.py (3.1.0) but differs on these inputs: (a) a ledger line `null` becomes an empty finding with no warning; (b) duplicate ledger ids are listed once per record, while findings.py keeps the last; (c) a top-level `location` in a ledger record is ignored (findings.py reads `rec.get("location") or extra.location`); (d) the ledger is split on `\n` only, not like `str.splitlines`; (e) encoding/json matches keys case-insensitively, so `{"ID":…}` loads; (f) `\r\r\n` in a finding file becomes a paragraph break, because splitLines splits the `\r\n` left after `ReplaceAll` twice; (g) `strings.TrimSpace` does not trim U+001C-U+001F as Python's `strip()` does; (h) `id: ""` falls back to the file name (`cmp.Or`), while findings.py uses "".

## Evidence

Reproduced against the current code: (a) `null` → finding id "" status "" and no warning; (b) two records for id `a` → 2 findings; (c) `{"id":"a","status":"fixed","location":"x.go:3"}` → Location ""; (d) two records separated by `\r` → 0 findings and warning `resolved.jsonl:1: invalid character '{' after top-level value` (Python reads 2); (e) `{"ID":"a","STATUS":"fixed"}` → id a, status fixed; (f) body `"line1\n\nline2\n"` vs Python `"line1\nline2\n"`; (g) `severity: "high"` + U+001F → `"high"` with quotes kept, Python `high`; (h) id `x-1` vs Python "". Sites: load.go:131 `strings.Split(string(data), "\n")`, :136-137 `json.Unmarshal(…, &r)`, :151 `Location: r.Extra.Location`, :101 `cmp.Or(fm["id"], …)`; frontmatter.go:76-93 splitLines; frontmatter.go:40-44 TrimSpace.

## Impact

The browser shows a different store than nitpicker's own `findings.py list` for the same files: phantom empty rows (a), duplicated rows after a git merge of two resolves (b), missing locations (c), dropped or accepted records (d, e), altered bodies and values (f, g, h). The CLAUDE.md parity rule does not hold.

## Fix

(a) Skip with a warning any line whose first non-space byte is not `{`. (b) Keep the last record per id. (c) Add a top-level `location` field and use `cmp.Or(r.Location, r.Extra.Location)`. (d) Split the ledger with splitLines. (e) Decode into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and read exact keys. (f) Treat `\r` followed by `\n` as one boundary in splitLines. (g) Trim with `strings.TrimFunc(s, func(r rune) bool { return unicode.IsSpace(r) || r >= 0x1c && r <= 0x1f })`. (h) Use the stem only when the `id` key is absent. Add each case to the parser and loader table tests, with expected values taken from findings.py.

## Resolution
load.go: ledger split with splitLines; decodeRecord rejects non-object lines and reads exact keys through map[string]json.RawMessage; top-level location, else extra.location; last record per id wins; open-file id falls back to the stem only when the key is missing. frontmatter.go: splitLines treats \r\n as one break; pyStrip trims U+001C-U+001F like str.strip. Tests TestLoadLedgerParity (6 cases), TestLoadEmptyIDKeyKept, and two TestParseFinding cases with expected values from findings.py.
title: Store parsing diverges from findings.py on eight edge inputs

body:
## Problem

(a) list.FilterMatchesMsg carries no identity, and forward() hands every one to whichever picker is open, so results computed for a picker that was closed fill the next one. (b) The bubbles list binds AcceptWhileFiltering to tab, shift+tab, ctrl+k and ctrl+j as well as the enter/up/down that updatePicker intercepts; those four reach the list and switch it to FilterApplied, after which typed letters stop narrowing.

## Evidence

(a) Reproduced deterministically: open the lens picker, type `s` and hold its command, press esc, open the category picker, deliver the held message — the category picker shows `["  security (1)" "  docs (1)"]` (lens rows) and enter sets `category: security`. Happens when the filter command finishes after the following keys (keys arriving in one read, or the rescan reopen at rescan.go:63-65). (b) bubbles v2.2.1 list/keys.go:75-77 `AcceptWhileFiltering: key.WithKeys("enter", "tab", "shift+tab", "ctrl+k", "up", "ctrl+j", "down")`; updatePicker (model.go:346-382) intercepts only Accept (enter), Cancel (esc), Up (up, ctrl+p), Down (down, ctrl+n).

## Impact

(a) A facet gets set to another facet's value and the list shows nothing. (b) After an accidental tab the picker no longer narrows as the user types.

## Fix

(a) Give each picker a generation number; wrap the commands returned by the picker list so their FilterMatchesMsg carries it, and drop a message whose generation is not the open picker's. (b) In newPicker, `l.KeyMap.AcceptWhileFiltering.SetKeys()` (no keys) so only the model's own bindings leave typing mode. Tests for both.

## Resolution
picker.go: every picker command is wrapped by tagPicker with the picker's generation; updatePickerMsg drops messages of a closed or replaced picker. newPicker empties AcceptWhileFiltering. Tests TestPickerDropsResultsOfAClosedPicker and TestPickerKeepsNarrowingAfterTab.
title: Picker accepts a closed picker's filter results and leaves typing mode on tab

body:
## Problem

applyRescan replaces the store but re-renders neither the detail view nor the warnings view, and it rebuilds an open picker from scratch, discarding the text typed into it and its cursor.

## Evidence

rescan.go:61-65 `m.setStore(msg.store); m.reselect(id, status, index); if m.mode == modePicker { return m.openPicker(m.picker.facet) }` — no branch for modeDetail, and openPicker (model.go:334-342) starts a new, empty filter. m.detail (model.go:394-402) keeps pointing into the old findings slice. TestRescanRebuildsOpenPicker asserts the rebuild but not the typed text.

## Impact

After `r` (pressed in the list, then a view opened before the result arrives), the warnings view keeps listing the old warnings until a resize, and a picker the user was typing into resets to the full list.

## Fix

In applyRescan: when in modeDetail, re-resolve m.detail by id and status in the new findings (nil-safe for the warnings view) and call renderDetail(); when in modePicker, reopen it and replay the previous `FilterInput.Value()` with SetFilterText before returning. Tests for both.

## Resolution
rescan.go applyRescan: an open picker is rebuilt by reopenPicker with the typed text replayed (SetFilterText, then SetFilterState(Filtering)); an open detail view is re-resolved by id and status and re-rendered (refreshDetail), and the warnings view is re-rendered. Tests TestRescanKeepsPickerText and TestRescanRefreshesWarningsView.
title: A rescan leaves an open detail or warnings view stale and clears the picker's typed text

body:
## Problem

findStore continues to the parent directory whenever `os.Stat(candidate)` fails, whatever the error. A permission error on the project's own store is reported as a missing store, or silently resolved to an ancestor directory's store.

## Evidence

main.go:92 `if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && info.IsDir() { return candidate, nil }` — any other err falls through to `parent := filepath.Dir(dir)`. Scenario: `chmod 000 docs/audit` in the project → Stat of docs/audit/findings fails with EACCES → the walk continues; with no store above, the user gets `no docs/audit/findings in . or any directory above it`; with one above (e.g. a monorepo root), that store opens instead.

## Impact

The message misdirects the user away from the real cause, and in a nested layout the wrong project's findings are shown with no indication.

## Fix

Stop at the first error that is not fs.ErrNotExist: `info, err := os.Stat(candidate); if err == nil && info.IsDir() { return candidate, nil }; if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) { return "", err }`. Add a test with an unreadable docs/audit (skipped when running as root or on Windows).

## Resolution
main.go findStore: only fs.ErrNotExist and ENOTDIR move the search up; any other Stat error is returned. Tests TestFindStoreReportsStatErrors (symlink loop, ELOOP) and TestFindStoreSkipsFileNamedDocs (a file named docs still walks up). GOOS=windows go vet clean.
title: findStore treats every Stat error as "no store here" and keeps walking up

body:
## Problem

mise.toml pins goreleaser 2.18.3, the version `goreleaser check` and snapshot builds use locally, but the release job asks goreleaser-action for `version: "~> v2"`, the newest v2 release at tag time.

## Evidence

mise.toml:20 `goreleaser = "2.18.3"`; release.yml:42-44 `uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@a4f02ab5… # v7.3.0` with `version: "~> v2"`. The other CI tools come from mise.toml through mise-action (ci.yml), so this is the one release-path tool that floats.

## Impact

The signed release can be built by a goreleaser that was never run against .goreleaser.yaml locally; a deprecation or behaviour change in a new v2 minor (archive naming, signing, extra_files) changes or breaks a release with no commit in this repository.

## Fix

Set `version: "v2.18.3"` in release.yml and keep it in step with mise.toml (bump both in one commit; a Renovate customManager or a `# renovate:` comment can track the release.yml value).

## Resolution
release.yml goreleaser-action version: "v2.18.3", the mise.toml pin, with a comment to bump both together; CLAUDE.md Build & Release says the same. goreleaser check exit 0; actionlint and zizmor pass.
title: Release builds with whatever goreleaser v2 is current, not the pinned 2.18.3

body:
## Problem

The test job gates golangci-lint, race tests and the build; markdownlint, yamllint, actionlint, zizmor, editorconfig-checker, shellcheck and the pre-commit-hooks set run only in the local prek hook, which each clone must install with `mise run hooks:install`.

## Evidence

ci.yml:45 `run: mise run lint`, :48 `run: mise run test-race`, :51 `run: mise run build`, :75 `run: go test ./...`, :94 `run: mise run vuln` — no `mise run lint:all`. During this project's implementation editorconfig-checker rejected 144 lines of docs/plans/2026-10-23-findings-store-tui.md and markdownlint reported 4 MD038 errors; both surfaced only when prek ran.

## Impact

A change from a clone without the hook (or a GitHub web edit) merges with editorconfig, markdown, YAML, workflow-lint or zizmor violations; the configuration encodes checks nothing enforces.

## Fix

Add a step `- name: Lint (pre-commit hooks)` / `run: mise run lint:all` to the test job after mise-action; prek is pinned in mise.toml and the checkout has tracked files for `--all-files`.

## Resolution
ci.yml test job: new step "Lint (pre-commit hooks)" running mise run lint:all after golangci-lint. actionlint and zizmor pass on it.
title: CI does not run the pre-commit hygiene hooks

body:
## Problem

Every remote hook repository is pinned by a tag (`rev: v6.0.0`, `v0.49.1`, `v1.38.0`, `v1.7.12`, `v1.31.1`, `v0.11.0.1-1`, `v4.0.2`). prek clones and executes that code on each developer's machine at commit time; a tag can be moved to different code.

## Evidence

.pre-commit-config.yaml `rev:` values are all tags; the GitHub Actions in .github/workflows are pinned by commit SHA with the tag as a comment (zizmor and checkov pass on them), so the hooks are the one executed third-party code not pinned by content. `prek autoupdate --help` documents `--freeze: Store "frozen" hashes in rev instead of tag names`.

## Impact

A compromised or re-tagged upstream hook repository runs arbitrary code in every contributor's checkout on the next commit, with no change in this repository to review.

## Fix

`mise exec -- prek autoupdate --freeze`, which rewrites each `rev` to a commit SHA with the tag as a comment, then `mise run lint:all` to confirm the hooks still pass.

## Resolution
prek autoupdate --freeze: every rev is now a commit SHA with "# frozen: <tag>"; the tags are unchanged (no version bump). All hooks pass on all 50 project files.
title: Pre-commit hook repositories are pinned by mutable tags

body:
## Problem

The project's binding agent rules ("Never write the store", "Never execute programs at runtime", sanitize at load, stdlib-only internal/findings) live in "## Rules that are easy to break", which starts at line 47 of 91 — after "## Development Commands" and "## Architecture", both lookup material. A critical rule placed mid-file is the one an agent skims past.

## Evidence

np_check_agent_instructions (lens AUD:A2) reports position_risk on CLAUDE.md line 55 (61%): "- **Never write the store.** Everything below `main` gets an `fs.FS`." Re-read: section headings are at lines 6 (Project), 13 (Development Commands), 31 (Architecture), 47 (Rules that are easy to break), 82 (Build & Release); "Never execute programs at runtime" is at line 78.

## Impact

An agent editing internal/findings or the loader can act on the architecture summary before reaching the constraints that forbid writing the store, executing programs, or importing non-stdlib modules — the rules most expensive to break here.

## Fix

Move the whole "## Rules that are easy to break" section to directly after "## Project" (line 6), ahead of "## Development Commands" and "## Architecture". No wording change is needed; re-run np_check_agent_instructions and confirm position_risk is gone.

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md: "Rules that are easy to break" moved directly after "Project", with the two "Never" rules first. np_check_agent_instructions reports 0 findings.
title: CLAUDE.md puts its hard rules after two sections of reference material

body:
## Problem

Finding class: dependency-vulnerability. The binary links golang.org/x/net v0.39.0 (indirect: glamour → bluemonday → golang.org/x/net/html), a version with 15 known advisories. Nothing in go.mod raises it above the version bluemonday requires.

## Evidence

Detecting tools: grype 0.120.1 (`grype dir:.`) and govulncheck 1.9.0 (`-show verbose`). go.mod:38 `golang.org/x/net v0.39.0 // indirect`. Advisories (grype severity, first fixed version): GO-2026-6612 Critical 0.60.0; GO-2026-4918 High 0.53.0; GO-2026-5026 High 0.55.0; GO-2026-6603 High 0.60.0; GO-2026-6611 High 0.60.0; GO-2026-5942 High 0.56.0; GO-2026-6617 High 0.60.0; GO-2026-6610 High 0.60.0; GO-2026-4440 Medium 0.45.0; GO-2026-4441 Medium 0.45.0; GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw Medium 0.55.0; GO-2026-5025/5027/5029/5030 Medium 0.55.0. `go mod why -m golang.org/x/net`: internal/ui → charm.land/glamour/v2/ansi → github.com/microcosm-cc/bluemonday → golang.org/x/net/html. govulncheck symbol analysis reports none of them called from this code today; trivy (errored: vulnerability DB download failed) did not run.

## Impact

The vulnerable module ships inside every release binary. Reachability is a property of today's call graph: any change that routes more of the rendered markdown through bluemonday's HTML parsing, or a glamour upgrade that does, can make a vulnerable function reachable with no go.mod change to flag it, and scanners that do not reason about reachability (grype, Dependabot/Renovate security alerts) report the release as vulnerable now.

## Fix

`go get golang.org/x/net@v0.61.0 && go mod tidy` (v0.60.0 is the lowest version fixing all 15; v0.61.0 is current), then `mise run all` — the glamour rendering tests in internal/ui/detail_test.go exercise the bluemonday path — and re-run `grype dir:.` to confirm 0 matches for golang.org/x/net.

## Resolution
Correction to the note above: the module is golang.org/x/net.
